about: The behavioural corpus for the bridge's PORT of the agent-board-toolkit's `kb_url_host` — the parser that turns a kanban API base into the BOARD-INSTANCE key a coord roster's `kanban_user_id` object is keyed by (card#10868 / card#10869). The toolkit OWNS the rule; the bridge copies it because it reads each agent's kanban user id out of that roster in PHP, at runtime (card#11172 / DL-450). tests/Unit/Support/KanbanInstanceKeyParityTest.php runs every vector against the port on every test run; bin/kb-owner-parity.sh runs the same vectors against a toolkit checkout's own `kb_url_host`.

authority.relationship: The toolkit OWNS this rule (its README § "The card owner — the kanban assignee" names it as the key of the roster's kanban_user_id object). A disagreement is the bridge's defect to fix by re-porting, never the toolkit's to fix by matching the bridge.

how_the_far_end_runs_this: From a bridge checkout: `bin/kb-owner-parity.sh --corpus docs/kb-instance-key-parity-corpus.json --toolkit <toolkit checkout>`. It sources that checkout's bin/_kb-board-lib.sh and gives every vector's single argument to `kb_url_host`; the printed host must equal `expect` byte-for-byte. Exit 0 agreed, 1 drifted, 2 could not measure. `--control` perturbs every expectation and must report each one.
not_checked_by_this_repo: NOTHING IN THIS REPO'S CI RUNS THE TOOLKIT: a change to `kb_url_host` reds nothing here until someone runs bin/kb-owner-parity.sh against the changed toolkit. Run it on a toolkit bump.
The check is VECTOR-granular: a toolkit change that moves no published vector is invisible to both ends.

As a discrimination check the runner was also run against a copy of the same lib with the trailing-dot strip removed and the id floor lowered to 0, and reported those vectors DISAGREE.
